1950.0: loft hatch open all week, did much warmth escape the house?
1950.1: bedroom an icebox so plenty, at least your husband goes up the loft.
1950.2: took the ladder away as a protest, one way to stop being asked.
1950.3: shut within the hour and the bedroom habitable again, victory at last.

1951.0: tried a new bakery on the high street, what did you pick up?
1951.2: croissant was worth it, the wait was not, go at seven next time.

1952.0: recycling collection changed colour, blue bin only now, what about the green ones?
1952.1: collected separately since the council split the contract, nobody told you.
1952.2: two weeks running and the neighbours very patient, they did not report you.

1953.0: front door lock sticking every damp morning, try graphite powder not oil.
1953.1: opposite of what you assumed, any hardware shop, a few quid for graphite.

1954.0: neighbour's kid started a car washing round, how much is he charging?
1954.2: saturday morning and the car not that clean since last summer, good lad.

1955.0: chimney smoke from next door already, they are keen, it is barely october.
1955.2: lovely and the woodpile stacked in september, they deserve the smoke.

1956.1: boiling water trick versus citric acid, mine preferred the citric acid treatment.
1956.2: worth a go before buying new, a fiver of descaler saves forty quid.

1957.0: winter duvet out of the vacuum bags, the changeover weekend, a milestone.
1957.1: smells of the loft, a day on the line sorts it, drying weather?

1958.0: lost the tv remote for three days, how did you survive?

1959.0: clock change next weekend and already dreading it, dark afternoons are the worst.
1959.1: night by half four so a daylight lamp, do they actually work?

1960.1: asked to join the teachers' team, intimidating, they will have all the answers.
1960.2: geography teacher put lisbon in spain last year, legendary, you could win.

1961.0: car booked for its mot four days before, cutting it fine.
1961.2: next week and both bulbs and the wiper replaced, veteran owner strategy.

1962.0: daughter wants to learn the guitar, how old is she?

1963.1: four buttons and none labelled, manual in a drawer somewhere, ours too.

1964.0: mum doing her christmas shopping already in october, she does this every year.
1964.1: everything wrapped by november, she calls it stress avoidance, sounds like wisdom.
1964.2: never noticing the cost in small slices, there is a lesson in that.

1965.0: fog came down thick this morning, was it the same your way?
1965.1: forty metres visibility on the bypass, everyone crawling together, oddly calm.
1965.2: gone by ten like it was never there, the whole morning a dream.
